evidence.design: White document rail without grey thumbnail frames; existing Manrope, teal and 44px outline controls. Minimal viewer uses the existing transparent blurred overlay, one document, zoom, close, previous, next and a counter.
verified: Mouse grab scrolls the rail without accidentally opening a document; an ordinary click opens the selected certificate.
The rail advances automatically at a four-second interval and pauses on hover. Manual pause changes to a resume control.
Dragging the open certificate switches documents. Zooming permits mouse panning; Home and ArrowLeft wrap from the first document to the last.
Clicking the document itself keeps the viewer open. Escape closes it, restores opener focus and restores body scrolling. Tab wraps from the last viewer control to zoom.
Mobile and tablet viewer images fit the available area; the short landscape layout moves controls beside the image. No horizontal page overflow at 390px or 320px.
TypeScript and targeted ESLint pass. The existing 64 pricing/rendering tests pass. All 184 WebP certificate assets are readable; certificate counts remain 23, 0, 42 and 27.

Independent code review confirmed gesture cleanup after pointer cancellation, window blur, release outside the stage and mouse movement without a pressed button. Pointer capture begins only after the drag threshold.
No new library or image assets were added for this revision. Full-size certificate loading remains limited to the open document.
codeReviewed: Autoplay also pauses while focus is within the gallery, during interaction, while the viewer is open, while the tab or gallery is not visible, and for reduced-motion preference.
Touch scrolling remains native in the rail; the viewer supports horizontal swipes without preventing pinch zoom or native vertical gestures.
limitations: Physical touchscreen swipe and pinch gestures were not tested on a device; responsive viewport rendering and touch handling code were checked.
An existing Next.js development CSP issue badge remains unrelated to this change. No production deployment was performed.
